title: Integrate Liquity V1 Stability Pool for LUSD Collateral Yield
body:
## Problem
Plain LUSD collateral earns 0% yield. Integrate Stability Pool for ~6.28% APR ([Dune data](https://dune.com/liquity/liquity-v1)) to fund governance token buybacks, without disrupting liquidity.

## Solution
Add `StabilityPoolFacet` via diamond proxy. Auto-deposit LUSD to pool on mint; withdraw principal on redeem. Harvest ETH/LQTY yields during redeems for buybacks/compounding (protocol-owned only). Piggyback ops on user txs for gas efficiency.

## Alternatives Considered
- AAVE (~3.24% yield, more complex).
- Leverage/LPs (higher risk).
- V2 migration (future option for multi-collateral).

## Implementation Spec
### ~~Prerequisites~~
- ~~Audit facet (~$10-20K budget).~~
- ~~Integrate `IStabilityPool.sol` (address: 0x66017D22b0f8556afDd19e1e5b5f1cbD89a6C337).~~
- ~~Add 1inch/Uniswap for swaps.~~
- ~~New storage: `totalPrincipalInPool` (uint256), `protocolTreasury` (address).~~

### Facet Functions
- `depositToPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `provideToSP(amount, address(0))`.
- `withdrawFromPool(uint256 amount)`: Call `withdrawFromSP(amount)`.
- `harvestRewards()`: Claim rewards, swap (e.g., 50% to LUSD for compounding, 50% to governance token for buybacks).

### Flows
- **Mint**: Transfer LUSD → Deposit to pool → Mint uUSD → Update `totalPrincipalInPool += amount`.
- **Redeem**: Burn uUSD → Calc principal → Withdraw/transfer principal → Harvest if rewards > threshold (route to treasury) → Update `totalPrincipalInPool -= amount`.

### Over-Collateralization
Value pool as LUSD equivalent (Chainlink oracles for ETH/LQTY). Redemptions: principal only.

### Monitoring/Automation
- Chainlink/Gelato for optional harvests. It would be nice to sell the ETH/LQTY for LUSD and boost holdings as soon as it is rewarded by the stability pool.
- Dune alerts for APR/supply.

## Testing
- Unit: Deposit/withdraw/harvest (Foundry).
- Integration: Mainnet fork; simulate liquidations.
- Edges: Low liquidity, volatility, mass redeems. Gas: <200K extra per tx.

## Deployment
1. Deploy facet.
2. `diamondCut` via multisig.
3. Verify on Etherscan.
4. Phased: Opt-in for new deposits.

## ~~Risks/Mitigations~~
- ~~Yield variability: Fallback to plain LUSD if APR <3%.~~
- ~~Supply crunch: Auto-withdraw if < $10M.~~
- ~~Security: Audit for reentrancy.~~

title: Staking v2 production deploy
body:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/994

We should deploy staking feature to production.

What to do:
1. Make sure the latest https://github.com/foundry-rs/foundry is installed
2. Make sure you're on the latest `development` branch of https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar
3. Make sure the `packages/contracts/.env` file contains the `OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY` env variable (which is the private key for the `ubq.eth` address which has both the `owner` and `admin` roles):
```
# Owner private key (grants access to updating Diamond facets and setting TWAP oracle address).
OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY="OWNER_PRIVATE_KEY"
```
4. From the `packages/contracts` folder run:
```
forge script migrations/mainnet/Deploy002_Staking.s.sol:Deploy002_Staking --rpc-url https://mainnet.gateway.tenderly.co --broadcast -vvvv
```
5. Commit broadcast logs

It seems this task is for @0x4007

title: Staking v2 audit
body:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/issues/985

We must audit the newly created staking contracts.

Scope:
1. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/StakingFacet.sol
2. https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibStaking.sol

Staking use case example for an end user:
1. User [stakes](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/StakingFacet.sol#L64) `LUSD/UUSD LP` tokens from [Curve pool](https://etherscan.io/address/0xcc68509f9ca0e1ed119eac7c468ec1b1c42f384f) 
2. Some time passes
3. User [unstakes](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/facets/StakingFacet.sol#L69) position and collects [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0) rewards

Notes:
- Staking code is based on [MasterChef](https://github.com/sushi-labs/sushiswap/blob/271458b558afa6fdfd3e46b8eef5ee6618b60f9d/contracts/MasterChef.sol)
- Auditor should consider how the staking feature works in context of the diamond pattern and [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) where users are able to:
  a) send [LUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0x5f98805a4e8be255a32880fdec7f6728c6568ba0) and [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0) in order to mint [UUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb6919Ef2ee4aFC163BC954C5678e2BB570c2D103)
  b) redeem [UUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb6919Ef2ee4aFC163BC954C5678e2BB570c2D103) in order to get [LUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0x5f98805a4e8be255a32880fdec7f6728c6568ba0) and [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0)

I suppose staked token must never be the same one used as collateral in [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) because it may skew calculations [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L354) and [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/ac517749fdddef3b9755c305224e2aacf14b7756/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L717).

title: Add `UUSD` and `UBQ` tokens to popular services
body:
Right now when you interact with DEXes or web3 wallets you have to paste UUSD/UBQ addresses manually in order to interact with those tokens. 

We should make sure that [UUSD](https://etherscan.io/address/0xb6919Ef2ee4aFC163BC954C5678e2BB570c2D103) and [UBQ](https://etherscan.io/address/0x4e38D89362f7e5db0096CE44ebD021c3962aA9a0) tokens are displayed "natively" in popular services in order to put less friction on our users.

  - https://bridge.gnosischain.com (contacted support)
  - https://app.debridge.finance (contacted support)
  - https://jumper.exchange (contacted support)
  - https://app.shapeshift.com (token list is taken from https://www.coingecko.com)
  - https://www.bungee.exchange (token list is taken from https://www.coingecko.com)

title: CI: fix `check_storage_layout` for new contracts
body:
There's the [core-contracts-storage-check](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/core-contracts-storage-check.yml) workflow which checks that contracts' storage is not messed on contract upgrades.

Check these CI runs which fails with the `No workflow run found with an artifact named...` error:
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/11125075713/job/30912062971?pr=959
- https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/actions/runs/11145695030/job/30975996318?pr=971

The issue is that when a **new contract** is added the [core-contracts-storage-check](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/core-contracts-storage-check.yml) starts to fail while the expected behavior for the CI workflow to pass because we don't need to check storage layout for newly added contracts (because storage of the newly added contract hasn't been updated hence storage collision could not occur).

So as a part of this issue we should make sure that:
1. [core-contracts-storage-check](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/core-contracts-storage-check.yml) is not failing for newly added contracts
2. [diamond-storage-check.yml](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/20799bedf5ee4d40d2863653f7bc2fe68a2ce3fa/.github/workflows/diamond-storage-check.yml) is not failing for newly added libraries

P.S. Pls provide a QA in the related PR with these scenarios:
1) No storage updates, CI passing
2) Storage update, no collision, CI passing
3) Storage update, collision, CI failing
4) New contract added, CI passing

title: Adding collateral enabled checks for redemption collections might make users uncapable of redeming their funds.
body:
[MEDIUM] - Adding collateral enabled checks for redemption collections might make users uncapable of redeming their funds.

This PR is intended to fix [the bug described in this Sherlock issue](https://github.com/sherlock-audit/2023-12-ubiquity-judging/issues/29). However, the Sherlock report is actually wrong and the vulnerability described must not be considered as an issue in the first place, so the collateralEnabled check should not be added on collecting redemptions.

Enabling/disabling collaterals allows the protocol to add or remove supported collaterals, not to be used under uncertain situations, such as a hack. In such type of situations, the `isRedeemPaused` check can be enabled to prevent users from redeeming if something wrong is currently  happening.

The problem with adding the `collateralEnabled` check here is that if Ubiquity decides to disable a collateral in the future, some redemptions might be already queued, so users won't be able to withdraw their funds.


Recommendation: Remove the `collateralEnabled` check for collecting redemptions.

_Originally posted by @0xadrii in https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/pull/894#discussion_r1572571068_

title: Security monitoring
body:
In case of a security incident we should:
1. Pause all of the contracts
2. Notify the core team that something went wrong

Possible solutions for monitoring:
- https://docs.chain.link/chainlink-automation
- https://www.openzeppelin.com/defender
- https://cyvers.ai/

What should be done:
1. Setup monitoring for [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol). [^01^]                                                                                                 In case of a possible security incident (let's say >30% of liquidity is withdrawn) we should:
a) Pause the [UbiquityDollarToken](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/core/UbiquityDollarToken.sol)
b) Pause [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) by [disabling collateral](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/a1b11e1b944227144d7cc19ab320220d9fce8b69/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol#L1129)
2. Send notification to https://t.me/UbiquityDAO (you may create a new topic there like `Dollar monitoring`)

P.S. Mainnet contract addresses can be found [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/e4c1fae5ef5e9ba40bcb84c671f2ba39f0ab5208/packages/contracts/broadcast/Deploy001_Diamond_Dollar_Governance.s.sol/1/run-latest.json)

title: Graph Compounding
body:
I'm focusing on the "breakeven line" idea and its ability to accurately express when a position is compounded (yield is withdrawn, and redeposited.) Instead of graphing it as a ray (a line with one "extended" point) we can instead graph it as a line segment (no extended points) from the position deposit time, to when a position's size is modified. 

If we add to the position size, then the breakeven line should be steeper (more fees should be accrued due to a larger position size.) I made a quick mockup using TradingView to illustrate this idea.

title: Dynamic Data Input
body:
# Dynamic Data Input on TradingView Indicator

The first major engineering challenge in order for this to be useful in realtime decision making is to allow for the script to have the capability to dynamically read position data from external data sources. I did quite a bit of research on this, and it appears that TradingView's PineScript does not currently have this capability. 

Currently the variables must be manually input on the indicator. This can be done by double clicking the indicator on TradingView.

![tv](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4975670/201572439-f6443b3e-5f1c-4abc-bc15-e8a0be86a129.jpg)

Those variables are manually imported off of the data presented by Revert's UI

https://revert.finance/#/uniswap-position/mainnet/312741

The founder of Revert passed me along this draft documentation of their private API. This was current as of 12 July 2022, as such there may have been some changes introduced since. This will allow you to access the information in JSON format. 

[apidocs.md](https://github.com/ubiquity/uniswap-v3-liquidity-provider-indicator/files/9999366/apidocs.md)

---

# Research

I would encourage you to explore workarounds.

### Workaround Strategy A - API Reverse Engineering

I would highly recommend API reverse engineering so that there is FAR LESS infrastructure to support for this capability. Then we could have a super simple node program that simply pings Revert (GET) and TradingView (POST) APIs every minute or so.

### Workaround Strategy B - Scraper

Have a remote invoked [scraper](http://github.com/ubiquity/scraper) to manually log in to your TradingView account, and

1. pass in the updated parameters using the settings panel (this might be possible by directly making the API request to update the user's settings vs having to navigate through the UI) or 
2. to hardcode the parameters and update the PineScript code.

title: Migrate backend to Deno-native + harden Deno Deploy
body:
Context
- Current backend uses Node-specific server (`@hono/node-server`) and `process.env` while deploying on Deno Deploy. This couples Node APIs to a Deno runtime and increases risk of incompatibilities and subtle failures.
- We already deploy via GitHub Actions OIDC to Deno Deploy (project: `pay-ubq-fi`). Frontend is built to `frontend/dist` and served by `backend/server.ts`.

Goals
- Run fully Deno-native on Deploy (no Node server adapter).
- Keep GitHub Actions deploy unchanged except for necessary tweaks.
- Preserve API behavior and static asset serving.

Scope of Work
- Replace server bootstrap with Deno-native:
  - Swap `@hono/node-server` + `serveStatic` for `Deno.serve` + `hono` fetch handler.
  - Use `Deno.env.get()` for configuration.
  - Serve SPA assets from `./frontend/dist` (index.html fallback).
- Supabase client
  - Import via `npm:@supabase/supabase-js` under Deno.
  - Validate ESM usage works on Deploy.
- Add `/health` endpoint returning 200 with basic info (uptime/version).
- Add `deno.jsonc` (server side) with:
  - `tasks` (dev/start/test)
  - Optional import map for `npm:` spec
  - Lint/fmt config
- CI/CD (pay.ubq.fi/.github/workflows/deploy.yml)
  - Keep OIDC deployctl step; ensure `entrypoint: backend/server.ts` still correct after refactor.
  - Ensure frontend build step remains and artifacts exist.
- CORS:
  - Keep current permissive CORS via `hono/cors` or stricter allowlist; document decision.
- Logging:
  - Ensure console logs appear in Deno Deploy logs; standardize error handling.

Acceptance Criteria
- No usage of `@hono/node-server` or `process.env` in runtime code.
- Server starts with `Deno.serve` and exports `app.fetch` handler.
- `GET /health` returns 200 JSON `{ status: "ok" }`.
- Static assets served from `frontend/dist`, SPA fallback serves `index.html`.
- Supabase calls succeed using `Deno.env.get` variables: `SUPABASE_URL`, `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`.
- CI deploy completes via `denoland/deployctl@v1` to project `pay-ubq-fi`.
- Docs updated: .rules and docs/additional/deno-deploy-guide.md reference Deno-native server and env names.

Non-Goals
- Frontend functional changes.
- Schema or Supabase policy changes.

References
- Server: `backend/server.ts`
- CI: `.github/workflows/deploy.yml`
- Project rules: `.rules`
- Deploy guide: `docs/additional/deno-deploy-guide.md`

Test Plan
- Local: `deno run --allow-net --allow-read --allow-env backend/server.ts` and open site; verify `/api/permits/record-claim` and `/health`.
- Deploy: confirm Deploy logs, static assets, and API endpoints.

Owner/Timebox
- Est: 0.5–1 day. Assign to backend engineer familiar with Deno/Hono.

title: Cow Swap Cash Out
body:
I was doing some research on [implementing automated cowswap orders](https://github.com/0x4007/travel-stipend/blob/feat/auto-swap/src/cowswap-swap.ts) (they have an SDK) and I realize that we can do something pretty cool:

1. Only support settlements using UUSD. 
2. Allow the user to configure what asset they want to be paid in, it should be saved in localStorage. 
3. The cowswap quote can appear in place of the reward amount. For example, by default, loading the app for `100 UUSD` permit would show that. But if the user configured to get paid in USDT, then it might come out to something like `99.5 USDT`. The app will simply display `99.5 USDT` instead if their settings are set as such. 
4. The claim permit button would actually 1. invalidate their permit (if the wallet can afford the pay out) 2. initiate a cowswap order with the beneficiary address set to the permit beneficiary

Then now we can enforce people using UUSD in the backend but user facing they can receive rewards in any asset they want! 

I think this provides best of all worlds for users. For partners, we could charge a premium for them to use other tokens natively in the background etc.

title: Safe{Wallet} First Class Support on Gnosis Chain
body:
This solution isn't fully developed as it only works for a single chain, making it cumbersome for users if partners use different chains. Deploying a SAFE with the same address across multiple chains is challenging.

However, by adding a special feature for Gnosis Chain, which sponsors up to five transactions per hour, we can enhance the user experience by eliminating gas fee concerns.

This approach addresses our issues related to creating a faucet.

[More about gas fee sponsoring](https://help.safe.global/en/articles/59203-what-is-gas-fee-sponsoring)

### An idea for seamless UX: 

This may require generating a private signing key in browser, proposal [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/219). Once the signing key has been added to the user's SAFE as an authorized signer, it should be able to prompt the SAFE that new transactions are waiting to be approved. This would work well on mobile due to the push notifications SAFE produces when a signature request occurs. 

As for desktop I am not 100% sure.

The best part about this is that the gas fee will be sponsored, so the in browser signing key never has to hold any value.

title: Integrate Wallet Connect via Reown AppKit
body:
## Overview  
Enable seamless wallet connectivity in the dApp by integrating the Reown platform's AppKit toolkit, supporting wallet login, transaction approvals, and cross-chain interactions. This spec is focused on Ethereum-compatible chains using `WagmiAdapter`. The solution uses React/Next.js as the UI framework.

## Goals  
- Support secure wallet connections without exposing private keys  
- Provide users wallet management (login/logout, transaction signing)  
- Utilize Reown's AppKit for enhanced UX, security, and multi-chain support  

## Tools and Libraries  
- `@reown/appkit/react` - Core UI and functionality kit  
- `@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi` - Adapter for Ethereum EVM chains  
- `wagmi` - Ethereum hooks for React wallet management  
- `@tanstack/react-query` - Data caching and syncing (used by AppKit)  

## Setup Steps

### 1. Project Initialization  
- Use Reown’s CLI to bootstrap your AppKit integration:  
```bash
npx @reown/appkit-cli
```
- Select your project name, framework (React or Next.js), and network library (`wagmi` recommended for EVM).  
- Enter project folder and install dependencies:  
```bash
cd your-project-name
npm install
```

### 2. Register Your Project on Reown Cloud  
- Create a free account at [[cloud.reown.com](https://cloud.reown.com/)](https://cloud.reown.com)  
- Create a new AppKit project; obtain the **Project ID** for configuration  

### 3. Environment Configuration  
- Create a `.env` file at the root of your repo, add:  
```env
NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID=your-reown-project-id
```

### 4. AppKit Setup in Code  
- Create a config file (e.g., `config/index.tsx`) to set up AppKit with WagmiAdapter and chains:  
```tsx
'use client';

import { createAppKit } from '@reown/appkit/react';
import { WagmiAdapter } from '@reown/appkit-adapter-wagmi';
import { mainnet, arbitrum } from '@reown/appkit/networks';

const wagmiAdapter = new WagmiAdapter({
  projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID!,
  networks: [mainnet, arbitrum],
});

export const appKit = createAppKit({
  adapters: [wagmiAdapter],
  networks: [mainnet, arbitrum],
  projectId: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_PROJECT_ID!,
  metadata: {
    name: 'Your DApp Name',
    description: 'Description of your dApp',
    url: 'https://your-dapp-url.com',
    icons: ['https://your-dapp-url.com/icon.png'],
  },
  features: {
    analytics: true, // optional
  },
});
```

### 5. Wrap Your Application with AppKit Provider  
- In your React root component (e.g., `_app.tsx` for Next.js), wrap your app with AppKit’s provider for context management:  
```tsx
import { AppKitProvider } from '@reown/appkit/react';

function MyApp({ Component, pageProps }) {

}
export default MyApp;
```

### 6. UI Integration and Wallet Connect Button  
- Use hooks like `useAppKitAccount()` to query wallet connection state and provide connection UI  
- Build wallet connect/logout buttons in your UI, styled with Chakra UI components for consistency  
- Example minimal connect button snippet:  
```tsx
import { useAppKitAccount, useAppKitModal } from '@reown/appkit/react';
import { Button } from '@chakra-ui/react';

function WalletConnectButton() {
  const { isConnected, disconnect } = useAppKitAccount();
  const modal = useAppKitModal();

  if (isConnected) {
    return Disconnect Wallet;
  }
  return  modal.open()}>Connect Wallet;
}
```

### 7. Handling Authentication & Transactions  
- Utilize AppKit hooks for transaction requests and approvals  
- Monitor wallet status and connect errors for UX feedback with UI toast notifications or modals  

### 8. Testing & Deployment  
- Test wallet connections on supported networks (e.g., Ethereum mainnet, Gnosis)  
- Test user flows: connect, disconnect, request signatures, transaction executions  
- Deploy with environment variables securely configured

title: Arbitrage bot
body:
In order to maintain [Dollar token](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/core/UbiquityDollarToken.sol) USD peg [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol) provides the following arbitrage mechanic:
1. If Dollar token USD price >1$ (on a secondary market) then arbitragers are incentivised to 
a) Mint 1 Dollar token for 1 USD of collateral in the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol)
b) Sell 1 Dollar token on a secondary market
2. On the contrary, If Dollar token USD price <1$ (on a secondary market) then arbitragers are incentivised to:
a) Buy cheap Dollar token on a secondary market
b) Redeem Dollar token for collateral worth 1 USD in the [LibUbiquityPool](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/src/dollar/libraries/LibUbiquityPool.sol)

On early project stage any large swap may affect the Dollar token price greatly and the pool (where the swap occurred) may remain unbalanced for a long time which in turn depegs the Dollar token.

As a part of this issue we should create an arbitrage bot (i.e. `nodejs` app) which could be run on VPS or any suitable PAAS (heroku, cloudflare, etc...) to catch arbitrage opportunities in order to keep the Dollar token USD pegged on early project stage.

What should be done:
1. Create a new `nodejs` app that will catch arbitrage opportunities for the Dollar token
2. Add unit tests for basic functionality
3. Prepare a clear README of how to run the bot

Notes:
- It makes sense to create the arbitrage bot in a separate repository.
- Deployed contract addresses (mainnet): [here](https://github.com/ubiquity/ubiquity-dollar/blob/0a230f977ad91bbfb01dd28bc1d2ea77faed5237/packages/contracts/broadcast/Deploy001_Diamond_Dollar_Governance.s.sol/1/run-latest.json)

title: V1: Backfill and validate historical permit payouts (GitHub + on-chain)
body:
## Goals

- Recover historical permit data from GitHub issues and comments.
- Rebuild permits into the current schema and de-duplicate against the database.
- Validate remaining permits against on-chain activity on Ethereum and Gnosis.
- Produce a final report of matched, withdrawn, and unresolved permits.
- Improve the foundation of the XP system
- have near complete auditability with 1:1 ratio of `issue label totals == stored permit totals`, or at the very least, each task having verified/tracked payouts

***

## Scope

### 1. Scrape and reconstruct permits

- Enumerate all Ubiquity-owned GitHub orgs and repositories.
- For each issue:
    - Filter comments created by the `prod` & `dev` UbiquityOS.
    - Extract any base64-encoded permit URLs from comment bodies.
    - Decode the base64 payloads and rebuild permit objects into the current expected shape.
- Exclude any permits that already exist in the production database.


### 2. Ad-hoc / manual permits

- In addition to bot comments, include comments by:
    - `@0x4007` for manually sent claim URLs when the bot was down or broken (personally happened to me).
    - `@gentlementlegen` where claim URLs may have been copy-pasted manually when things were down/broken (I'm positive I saw it happen for another contributor, if not myself).
- Parse and process these comments for claim URLs using the same pipeline as bot comments.
- Treat these as best-effort coverage to improve audit completeness.


### 3. Permit validity checks

- For all reconstructed permits not already in the DB:
    - Check on-chain whether the permit nonce has been invalidated.
        - Case A: The permit was claimed by the `beneficiary`.
        - Case B: The signer invalidated/withdrew the permit via the `owner` address.
- If claimed:
    - Match the permit directly to an on-chain transaction involving the `beneficiary`.
- If not claimed:
    - Attempt to locate the invalidation transaction from the `owner` address; otherwise classify as “assumed withdrawn”.

***

## On-chain validation (Ethereum + Gnosis)

Both options require mapping `beneficiary` addresses to users in the production DB.

### Common requirement

- Map `beneficiary` → user by:
    - Using the current wallet mapping in the production DB where possible.
    - Where mappings have changed, parse the `username` from the original bot permit comment to resolve historical ownership.


### Option A: CSV-based, thresholded

- Group reconstructed permits by `beneficiary` address and sum total amounts.
- Exclude addresses with a total under a configurable threshold (e.g. 1,000 USD equivalent).
- For remaining addresses:
    - Manually export transaction history CSVs from Etherscan and GnosisScan.
    - Parse CSVs and group transfers that match `permit transfer from` patterns from known funding wallets.
- Accept that low-earning contributors below the threshold may remain unresolved.


### Option B: Programmatic, full coverage

- Build a structure such as `Record<IssueUrl, Array<{ ...Permit, txHash }>>`.
- For each distinct wallet address:
    - Page through full transaction history from RPC / explorer APIs.
    - Attempt to match permit parameters to on-chain call arguments or transfer patterns.
- For permits without an associated transaction hash:
    - Group them by contributor and issue.
    - Enforce that each contributor can only successfully claim once per issue.
    - Write leftover unmatched permits to a file for manual inspection.
- Store matched permits (with tx hash) keyed by issue/repo/org.

***

## Scale / complexity

- Expected scale: thousands of transactions and hundreds of missing permits.
- Non-trivial data volume and debugging effort across:
    - GitHub API scraping and parsing.
    - Base64 decoding and schema normalization.
    - On-chain history queries on two networks.
    - Heuristic matching and manual review for edge cases.

title: Make text-conversation-rewards MCP Compliant
body:
To enable broader interoperability, we should make the `text-conversation-rewards` plugin MCP compliant. This would allow any LLM or external system to interact with it using the Model Context Protocol, rather than relying on UbiquityOS-specific conventions.

### Key Points & Discussion

- **MCP Integration:**  
  Use the [typescript-sdk](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk) for standard MCP integration. This may require changes to the `manifest.json` schema or an adapter for compatibility.

- **Deployment:**  
  All plugins should have a Deno Deploy endpoint. For plugins currently running as GitHub Actions, the Deno endpoint should trigger the Action (see [daemon-pricing](https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/daemon-pricing) for an example).

- **Streamable HTTP:**  
  MCP works through Streamable HTTP. Deno supports streaming, but it's not strictly required for all MCPs.

- **Context Handling:**  
  The main challenge is providing the necessary context (e.g., repo/issue/task info) when running outside GitHub (e.g., Telegram, CLI). Platform adapters may be needed to capture and provide this context.

- **Platform Agnosticism:**  
  `text-conversation-rewards` can be made platform-agnostic if we decouple content retrieval from GitHub and allow input from other sources (e.g., Google Docs, Telegram). The main non-agnostic part is currently content retrieval.

- **Standardization:**  
  Standardizing Deno deploy templates (similar to Cloudflare) will help. We have implemented some MCP-like standards already, but aligning with industry standards is beneficial.

- **Next Steps:**  
  - Prototype MCP compliance with `text-conversation-rewards` first.
  - Consider making a special AI system capability for plugins that use the current manifest format.
  - If successful, expand to other plugins as needed.

---

title: Migrate tests from Jest to Bun Test
body:
## Task: Migrate Test Suite from Jest to Bun Test

**Goal:** Replace the current Jest test runner setup with Bun's built-in test runner (`bun test`) for improved performance and simplified tooling.

**Context:**
This project currently uses Jest for running tests. Migrating to `bun test` aligns with the project's adoption of Bun for other tasks (runtime, package management) and can potentially offer faster test execution, plus should help us dealing with ESM import issues and required transformers.

**Required Changes:**

1.  **Remove Jest Dependencies:**
    *   Uninstall Jest-related packages (`jest`, `@types/jest`, `ts-jest`, `babel-jest`, `ts-node` etc.)
    *   Remove the `.babelrc` file
2.  **Remove Jest Configuration:**
    *   Delete the `jest.config.ts` file.
3.  **Update `package.json` Scripts:**
    *   Modify the test script(s) to use `bun test` instead of `jest`.
4.  **Refactor Tests:**
    *   Go through all files in the `tests/` directory.
    *   Replace Jest's global functions (`describe`, `it`, `test`, `expect`, `beforeEach`, `afterEach`, etc.) with imports from `"bun:test"`.
        ```typescript
        import { describe, it, expect, beforeEach, afterEach, mock } from "bun:test";
        ```
    *   Adjust test matchers as needed. While many are similar, there might be differences. Refer to the [Bun Test documentation](https://bun.sh/docs/test/writing).
    *   Update mocking logic. Replace `jest.mock`, `jest.fn`, `jest.spyOn` with Bun's mocking capabilities (e.g., `mock`, `spyOn` from `"bun:test"`).
    *   `mswjs` does not work with `bun` for network mocking. Consider looking into https://github.com/DRFR0ST/bun-bagel or mock Octokit altogether.
5.  **Verify:**
    *   Run `bun test` and ensure all tests pass successfully.
6.  **Update CI/CD:**
    *   Modify `jest-testing.yml` that execute tests to use the new `bun test` command.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

*   All Jest dependencies and configuration files are removed.
*   All tests in the `tests/` directory are successfully migrated to use `bun test` APIs.
*   `bun test` runs without errors and all tests pass.
*   CI/CD pipelines are updated to use `bun test`.

title: Implement Differential Reward Distribution for Reopened Issues
body:
When an issue is reopened and closed again, the reward system should calculate and distribute only the difference between previously granted rewards and new rewards.

**Requirements**:
1. Track Previous Rewards
   - Store transaction history with amounts per beneficiary
   - Record payment mode (direct/permit) used for each distribution

2. Differential Calculation
   - Compare new reward amounts with previously distributed amounts
   - Calculate positive differences only (additional rewards)
   - Skip beneficiaries with no change in rewards

3. Distribution Logic
   - Only process transactions for beneficiaries with positive reward differences
   - Handle cases where original payment failed but issue was reopened

4. Error Handling
   - Validate transaction history before processing
   - Handle missing or incomplete previous distribution data
   - Log detailed comparison between old and new reward amounts

**Technical Considerations**:
- Must not conflict with wallet insolvency fallback (generates permits if wallet can't afford payouts) 
- Extend Supabase schema to track complete distribution history
- Implement comparison logic in `payment-module.ts`
- Update GitHub comment format to show differential amounts

**Example Scenario**:
```typescript
// Original distribution
{
  "user1": { total: 100, paid: true },
  "user2": { total: 50, paid: true }
}

// New calculation
{
  "user1": { total: 150, difference: 50 },
  "user2": { total: 50, difference: 0 },
  "user3": { total: 25, difference: 25 }
}
```

**Success Criteria**:
- Only processes payments for positive differences
- Provides clear audit trail of all distributions
- Handles edge cases: failed payments, partial distributions should never happen with the insolvency fallback. 
- Handle what happens if we change the mode (direct, permits only) between distributions

title: Incentives for lower estimates
body:

As the DAO grows and trust naturally decreases, there should be an incentive for the author and possibly assignee for them to want to make time estimates for tasks as short as realistically possible (or just as close to accurate as possible)

Otherwise the natural incentive is to over estimate all tasks to make pricing larger than it should be. 

Currently the only soft incentive is the financier/admins/managers needing to approve a time estimate before "funding" tasks. 

#### time accuracy 

This is very tricky to do because even if it's a `<4 hour` task, in our system design it's perfectly acceptable to spread that project over a few days. Because of this, we can't simply check the timeline timestamps of when they started and when they pushed their last commit or comment to determine how long it actually took them. Finding accurate time estimates may be better suited for an LLM to be the judge but even still it might be tough to do with accuracy. RAG with all the comments in the repository may provide more clues/hints for accuracy but this still seems shaky. We could do an experiment with estimating time estimates based on RAG context and then we could consider a penalty/bonus depending on how aligned the estimate is for the LLM compared to who set the label?

It could even be revealed only when the project is closed as complete which may incentivize further the label setter to tell the truth. I.e. "accurate label set bonus reward" which can be a gradient based on how close in milliseconds the label value is to the LLM estimate.

title: Agentic exploration
body:
I’d like to propose enhancing the /ask plugin with agent-like capabilities, allowing the LLM to explore the repository, organization, or external resources as needed to answer a question more effectively.

For example, currently the LLM only has access to documents explicitly attached in the triggering comment. However, relevant information often exists elsewhere (such as in related issues/PRs, README, code files) that the LLM cannot currently access.

By enabling the LLM to explore more freely, we could greatly improve the quality and context-awareness of its responses.

The LLM agent could:
-	Access repo files: Fetch any file in the repo (e.g. source code, README, config files) to gain context.
-	Follow cross-references: Detect and fetch linked issues or PRs (e.g. `in #100 this was already implemented`) and retrieve their body or summarized comments.
-	Leverage external resources: Fetch linked documents or URLs from comments to extract additional context.
-	Explore related content: Automatically detect and pull in other relevant comments in the same issue that contain documents or links.

Use cases
-	When answering a question about a plugin, the LLM could fetch the README or main code file to better understand its purpose.
-	If someone references another issue (see #123), the LLM could fetch its description or comments to provide context.
-	If earlier comments contain documents or links, the LLM could use them even if they weren’t in the triggering comment.

Benefits
-	More complete and contextual answers
-	Reduced need for users to repeat or restate context
-	Smarter, more autonomous behavior aligned with how developers actually communicate

title: Nomic Embeddings Model for +10% Accuracy
body:
The vector embedding model that we use is slightly outdated. I did some research to see what has higher accuracy, and I found one with 10% increased accuracy. We should make use of it as well as our old model. 

## Leaderboard

Model | Top-5 Retrieval Accuracy (%) | Notes
-- | -- | --
Nomic Embed v1.5 | ~86.2% | Highest overall retrieval accuracy in semantic search benchmarks, especially strong on short & direct queries. Open source and highly accurate.
Voyage-3-large | ~75-77% | Best model from Voyage AI, state-of-the-art in industry, notably outperforms OpenAI text-embedding-3-large by ~9.7%. Strong on domain-specific tasks.

## Tradeoff

> When you submit a GitHub comment that exceeds the token capacity of the embedding model, typically:
> - The model will truncate the input at its token limit (e.g., 8,192 tokens for Nomic or 32,000 tokens for Voyage).
> - This means any text beyond the max token limit is ignored, which can lead to loss of context and reduced embedding quality if important content is cut off.

## Solution

> 2. Similarity Functions
> - Key Point: Embeddings from different models generally cannot be directly compared using the same similarity function (e.g., cosine or dot product) unless their vector spaces are aligned.
> - Each model produces numerical vectors in its own latent space, meaning the scale, direction, and semantic meaning may differ dramatically.
> - Comparing Nomic vectors against Voyage vectors directly will yield misleading results.
> 
> What To Do:
> - In practice, keep embeddings from each model in separate indices or collections.
> - For each query or search, use the correct index according to the embedding model used: maintain “Nomic space” and “Voyage space” separately.

## Remarks

GitHub comment limit is 65,536 characters ≈ 16,384 tokens (rough estimate.) This means that especially comments with metadata unlikely will be able to rely on Nomic (8,192 max tokens)

## Research

Task matchmaking will be very powerful when coupled with the `/start` logic in this plugin.   

The key magic of `/start` is that it is designed to check if the assignee is already saturated with work (i.e. [^01^]         two concurrent tasks max) or needs to place their attention on any existing open pull reviews etc. 

Task recommendation should have the ability to automatically assign team members based on how saturated they are. If for example the top three recommendations are 

1. [^05^]      gentlementlegen 
2. whilefoo 
3.  shiv810 

But gentlementlegen is already working on two projects concurrently, then the matchmaking should automatically go to the next suitable candidate, Whilefoo. 

The purpose of this proposal is so that we don't need to duplicate the logic in that plugin for matchmaking. [^02^]   Instead, we should expose an API to have this plugin compute whether gentlementlegen can start or not.  

1. Let's clone the `command-start-stop` repository as a submodule inside of the `text-vector-embeddings` repository and then invoke the logic locally. 
2. Let's add the capability to assign collaborators based on the output of start logic. [^04^] 

### cron future 

We can constantly check the saturation state of team members and when they finish a project they can be automatically assigned to any that need to be completed, in order of priority. Then the AI manager will always be pushing to get urgent tasks done. 

It will also intelligently not assign those who are already disqualified because that's also in the start logic! [^03^]

title: Improving Recommendations
body:
Cool to see it always recommends at least one person but it is very much not relevant. 

Whats the timeline looking like to populate the database by scraping the existing closed issues and their assignees @sshivaditya2019? 

### repo/org/global Context Matching

I think we should optimize our logic. Tasks that may look similar but posted in two different repositories may in reality be quite different. Normally I would prefer to matchmake against those who completed similar tasks within the same repository, but we can "fallback" to org context (try to matchmake against any repository's task in the org) and then a final "fallback" to global context. 

Perhaps the simplest way to calculate this could be to subtract relevance "points"

Example:
```
0% adjustment: Same repository matching percentage 
-25% adjustment: Same organization
-50%: Global
```

Meaning for an identical task posted in three different locations:
```
same repo = 100% match
same org, different repo = 75% match
different org = 50% match
```

Just an idea but open to discussing to make this more accurate and simple to implement. 

### Recent Code Changes Fallback

Another idea to always try and match somebody is to check how much of the codebase was authored by whom. If nobody hits a relevance of greater than 25% we can fallback to assigning whoever wrote most of the code in the repository. Surely we can find the stats somewhere. 

### Future Considerations

Because we want the system to always be assigning the right contributor at the right time in the future, we should consider the output of the `/start` command as well, with all its checks. If UbiquityOS is able to run `/start` on behalf of others this can solve most of the problems I can think of. 

Specifically, imagine the scenario where the same top contributor is always recommended to work on the newly posted tasks. [^05^] [^04^] [^03^] [^01^] With a concurrent task limit of 2, they will quickly be saturated with work. We should be able to detect this and fallback/recommend/assign the next best.

title: Codebase semantic search
body:
For on boarding new developers, or just to synchronize existing developers, we should be generating embeddings of our code base. We can do per file or on the function level, depending on which has better performance.

I asked GPT for the best sorting method on the [embedding leaderboard](https://huggingface.co/spaces/mteb/leaderboard). 

Later it clarified that we should be sorting by "retrieval with instructions" for best results. 

[FollowIR-7B](https://huggingface.co/jhu-clsp/FollowIR-7B) is the highest ranked. 

We should be doing this in two steps:
1. Primarily, we should be generating embeddings of the new files when pull requests are merged.
2. We should have a tool that we can run manually (manual dispatch on GitHub actions ok) to generate all the embeddings. This would be expected to be used if there were pushes directly to the default branch and were not added via pull request

### additional context

> For this use case (codebase question-answering), your focus should be on retrieval tasks. Based on the criteria provided, here’s how I would prioritize the metrics:

> 1. **Retrieval Average (15 datasets)**: This should be your highest priority. The better the retrieval capability of the model, the more relevant code chunks it will retrieve when you ask a question about the codebase.

> 2. **Embedding Dimensions**: A higher embedding dimension may provide more nuanced representations of code and questions, improving retrieval accuracy. However, this needs to be balanced with memory usage and model size.

> 3. **Model Size (Million Parameters)**: Larger models tend to perform better in generating high-quality embeddings, but at the cost of memory and speed. Consider how much memory and computational power you can afford.

> 4. **Max Tokens**: A higher max token limit is useful for code because some functions or files can be quite large. You'll want a model that can handle bigger chunks of code.

> 5. **Classification Average (12 datasets)**: Code-related tasks sometimes involve classification (e.g., determining the type of question or identifying sections of code). A higher classification score can help in such scenarios.

> 6. **STS Average (10 datasets)**: Semantic Textual Similarity (STS) is also important as it measures how well the embeddings capture semantic meaning, which is useful for understanding the context and retrieving the right code section.

> ### Sorting Criteria:
> Sort by **Retrieval Average** first, then consider **Max Tokens** and **Embedding Dimensions** for practical handling of code and performance optimization.

> The other metrics like **Classification**, **Clustering**, and **Reranking** are less critical for your specific use case, but they can help refine the quality if you have a secondary need for such tasks.

body:
> Could you can try running `/rewrite` on https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/issues/154 please?

> It meets all the criteria for it, and would be great to see it in action. (My concern is that it does not factor in the PR or any code at all, which is a huge amount of missing context as it's unreasonable to expect all technical details to be mentioned in the conversation but their acceptance by reviewers is specification discovery in and of itself)


As a contributor who over the years has often taken on ambiguous specs and saw them through to completion, it has been my experience that, oftentimes a lot of ambiguous specs shift product-design and engineering effort onto contributors and it often goes unrecognized the amount of work that gets put in.

For this plugin to work as best as it can it must also have context of the active PR because, in my experience, a lot of what I implement gets accepted without it being mentioned in the spec/issue convo. It only appears in conversation through review if it needs tweaked or rejected so this means:

- anything off-spec which is undiscussed (an inherent acceptance of that deliverable) is unknown to the llm
- it does not surface reviews or PR comments

Finally, it's unreasonable to expect (I think) contributors who have done the extra product-design and engineering work to list all tech specs of their implementation into the issue, before then calling `/rewrite`. Better UX if the plugin/agent handles this themselves.

One recent example (although there are tens more I could think of):

- https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/issues/154 - barren, very little activity, no discussion around my suggestions which have all been accepted at this point
- https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/command-start-stop/pull/185 - context rich, laden with activity, huge amount of undiscussed technical details that have been accepted, plenty of changes requested by reviewers

title: Enhance Kernel with Generalized Request Handling & Secure External API
body:
#### **Summary**  
Expand the kernel's ingress beyond GitHub webhooks by introducing a secure public API endpoint. This will allow external services to trigger GitHub Actions workflows, effectively turning Actions into a general-purpose backend.  

#### **Key Features**  
- **Public API Endpoint**:  
  - Accepts external requests to execute plugins via the kernel.  
  - Supports dynamic execution of actions, enabling broader integrations.  

- **Authentication & Security**:  
  - Requests must include:  
    - `installation ID` (this allows us to target the correct org)  
    - `repository ID` (optionally, to load a specific repo config)  
  - Partners must provide an **encrypted password** stored in their config.  
    - Uses **X25519 encryption** (same system as EVM private key storage).  
    - Clients pass a password in the request header, which the kernel decrypts.  
  - Rate-limiting to prevent abuse.  

- **Execution Flow**:  
  1. Kernel receives an authenticated request with at least `installation ID` and `password`.  
  2. It decrypts the password and verifies the request.  
  3. Executes the specified plugin and returns the response.  

- **Webhook Replies**:  
  - Requests can include a `response URL` header.  
  - The kernel posts the result from the action plugin to this URL upon completion.  

- **Future Enhancements**:  
  - Investigate **cross-plugin communication** via the kernel relay.  

#### **Next Steps**  
- Define API Contract (Headers, Payload Format)
- Implement Authentication & Decryption Logic
- Extend Kernel Request Handling to Invoke Plugins
- Add Support for Webhook Response Delivery

title: Plugin "Classes"
body:
It's slowly becoming clear that we have different categories of plugins that interoperate. Perhaps its worth formalizing the system architecture to support this concept. 

To clarify, the kernel should be a generalized webhook quarterback, capable of relaying any webhook to any plugin, based on the config of the organization. It should not be tied to GitHub only. 

Plugin Classes:

- Financial Incentives[^1^]
- Vector Embeddings[^2^]
- Model Context Protocol[^3^]

[^1^]: Currently known as `text-conversation-rewards` and with its "sub-plugins" these should always return a "reward request" which implies that it will give a financial reward to the user for doing something. 
[^2^]: We already have several "sub-plugins" that rely on a single vector embeddings database, such as `/ask`, `deduplication`, `/annotate` and `task-matchmaking`. 
[^3^]: This isn't clear to me if we should apply this on the kernel directly and/or on the `command-` and `daemon-` plugins OR if we should make another "Plugin Class" that has "sub-plugins" which are "MCP enabled".

title: Model Context Protocol Standard vs Manifests
body:
We reinvented the wheel, probably poorly, with our manifests and tool calling via LLMs. We can turn our kernel into a [MCP Client](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/quickstart/client) and the plugins into [MCP Servers](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/quickstart/server).

I was installing a bunch of MCPs for my Cline extension to use and was looking at some source code of an MCP:

https://github.com/ferrislucas/iterm-mcp/blob/961882be693b82e258408f24ca1f40ee0a96e033/src/index.ts#L25-L72

Looks familiar. 

We should adopt the MCP standard because 1. surely Anthropic did a better job designing the architecture 2. interoperability with [all the MCP tools](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/servers). There's a huge community already.

### Remarks

To be honest it isn't clear to me if we must make all of our plugins into MCP servers, or if we just make our kernel into an MCP server. 

I think there could be some real innovation here to support making Actions/Workers easily into hosted MCP servers with exposed endpoints. This means combining our plugin template with their MCP template. 


### Related

- https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/typescript-sdk?tab=readme-ov-file#low-level-server could be merged with our plugin template. This "low level server" looks awfully familiar to a Cloudflare Worker.

title: Callbacks - event handlers and hybrid plugins
body:
I want to improve the experience of setting up event handlers and hybrid plugins.
I imagine something like this

```js
.on("issue_comment.created", "action", handler1)
.on("issue.closed", "worker", handler2)
```

The SDK would handle calling the Action or run it normally as a Worker and in case you're running it locally it would execute Action handlers locally too. 
Sometimes the reason why we need to call it as an Action is because some libraries are not supported by CF Workers so it'd be also good to have an option to run it as an Action even if you're running it locally.
Current hybrid plugins use `ACTION_REF` to know which Action to call but it'd be great if we could somehow get it automatically but I realize that may be not feasible.

At this point I would also consider merging `createActionsPlugin` and `createPlugin` for seamless experience.

I also realized that maybe we don't need kernel credentials to trigger Action from the Worker but only a fine-grained Github token that would only have access to the repo. Because we don't change the payload but only forward it to the Action, we don't need to generate a new signature and we can keep the original.

Right now, each plugin posts comments on its own using Octokit. We should change this so the kernel posts comments for all the plugins. If we plan to do something like [this issue](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugins-wishlist/issues/54#issuecomment-2652784793), this change will be important.

Instead of each plugin creating a comment on its own, the plugin SDK should send the data to the kernel, and the kernel will handle creating the event.

title: Improve the tool calling
body:
Improve the tool calling approach by:

1. Switching to the `gpt4o` model for better performance on complex queries.
2. Using Few-Shot Examples (dynamic or static) with semantically similar examples to guide the model, improving accuracy by providing relevant context. Dynamic examples can adapt to user input for more precise responses. The plugins call examples would be semantically similar to input query to the command router.

title: Add support for calling worker plugins from URL set in the manifest
body:
Depends on https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/issues/33

[This](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/issues/33) task introduces a new property `homepage_url` (which is a plugin worker URL) in the [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/blob/8d8f06958ca1273f299ae0bc2a51a6c512411af9/manifest.json) file.  

The idea is that now the bot's config will contain only `org/repo` in the plugin's config. For example [here](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/.ubiquity-os/blob/67df7f5643edcaa3899304481f7ff4ef74a1041a/.github/.ubiquity-os.config.dev.yml#L3) instead of
```
- plugin: https://ubiquity-os-comment-vector-embeddings-development.ubiquity.workers.dev
```
we will set `org/repo` value:
```
- plugin: ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-vector-embeddings
```

The kernel should support calling a worker URL if it is set in the [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/blob/8d8f06958ca1273f299ae0bc2a51a6c512411af9/manifest.json).

How it is supposed to work:
1. If `plugin` config property contains URL then call it as a worker (this is to support close sourced plugins + for backwards compatibility)
2. If `plugin` config property contains `org/repo` value then fetch plugin's [manifest.json](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/blob/8d8f06958ca1273f299ae0bc2a51a6c512411af9/manifest.json):
  - If `homepage_url` property is present in the manifest then call the plugin as a worker
  - If `homepage_url` property is missing then call plugin as a github action

Original [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity-os/plugin-template/issues/33#issuecomment-2549092026)

title: Hitting rate limits on too many webhook requests
body:
There might be cases when the kernel receives too many webhook events, for example:
- [some](https://t.me/UbiquityDAO/29891/32505) file is deleted from all of the repos
- too many partners are using the `ubiquity-os` app

When the kernel receives too many webhooks it exceeds github API rate limits which causes the kernel to be unresponsive and throwing the `Rate limit hit with \"GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/contents/{path}\", retrying in 1469 seconds` error. 

There should not be any downtimes in the kernel work.

title: Follow redirects on plugin renaming
body:
Right now the kernel does not follow redirects if plugin repository name is updated.

Example: we've recently renamed https://github.com/ubiquibot/conversation-rewards to https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards and the kernel stopped calling https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards plugin although https://github.com/ubiquibot/conversation-rewards redirects to https://github.com/ubiquity-os-marketplace/text-conversation-rewards.

There should be either a separate option in `octokit` to follow redirects or we should manually check that if response is `302` then call a new plugin location.

Related [comment](https://github.com/ubiquity/pay.ubq.fi/issues/298#issuecomment-2418791399)

P.S. Chances are it is expected behavior for security reasons

title: SDK improvements
body:
The SDK could get some improvements to make it more friendly to use

- `"hono"` doesn't seem to be shipped with it but is required to serve the plugin, so it might be included, or even better, encapsulated within the SDK.
- there is `createPlugin` and `createActionPlugin`. Maybe we could have only `createPlugin`, that would change behavior depending on either the runtime or the environment (e.g. running on a Worker / Action). - now both Actions and Workers come with a manifest, and this doesn't seem to be currently available for `createActionPlugin` (might be solved if we merge both function).
- the validate and decode + inputs could be handled in the SDK (currently just Decodes with no error nor Default).
- expose the `postComment` methos to make sure we have metadata on the comments
- remove duplicated declaration of `postComment`
- improve logs for error (there is none at the moment)
- add GraphQL paginate to Octokit
- option to disable the signature check for ease of use locally

title: Decrypt sensitive config parameters
body:
Right now there are 2 ways to hide sensitive bot's config parameters:
1. Make a config repository private (organization collaborators can still see the values though)
2. Fork plugin, self host and set sensitive parameters in env variables (bad UX for partners)

Sensitive config parameters could be encrypted via our own `x25519_PUBLIC_KEY` (the same one we use for encrypting partners' private keys) and the kernel could then decrypt them.

So as a part of this issue the kernel should be able to decrypt config parameters on initial config parsing. 

The expected flow for parsing a single config param:
1. Try to decrypt the parameter. 
2. If it is decrypted then use the decrypted parameter.
3. If there's a decryption error then assume the parameter is not encrypted and use a raw value.

Notice that there is a difference between decrypting: 
1. Unencrypted param
2. Encrypted param with another PK

I hope https://doc.libsodium.org/ distinguishes those 2 errors because in the 2nd case it will be a very subtle bug and the kernel should ideally throw an error like `The config parameter encryption is invalid` so that partner knew he did something wrong on encrypting a param.

P.S. Handy tool: https://keygen.ubq.fi/

title: Automatic Transfer
body:
The permit generation plugin should also optionally be able to automatically invoke a transfer to the beneficiaries. 

This introduces additional complexities because it must be able to estimate the gas fee of the transaction (given that we must support multiple EVM networks, with varying levels of activity, it is not viable to hard code this.)

In an org/repo config we can have a property related to payments `transfer: true`

It should also allow for the kernel operator (@ubiquity) to take a fee[^1^]. This fee should be configured elsewhere, perhaps in Cloudflare Worker Secrets (partner projects should not be able to change this.) Any fees that we take should be direct transfers of Ubiquity Dollars to `ubq.eth`.

[^1^]: This means we have to start thinking about how to capture value from payments moving around in our system. I think that we need to make a superior developer experience with our SDK and permit requests, so that plugin developers can easily capture value from the transactions their plugins are helping with.

title: command-plan
body:
I was experimenting with allowing codex to plan sprints (post all the GitHub Issues with correct labels, parent/child issue relationships, and blocking/blocked by relationships) using the below prompt.

It works quite well and I think there is value to build this out as a capability for our manager. 

We can write /plan and it can take the spec and break it down into child issues. 

Although come to think of it, I think we should have another dedicated plugin for estimating time labels, meaning that this prompt should remove any label related operations if we do go with that approach. 


---

## GitHub Issues & Sprints

This project manages work via GitHub issues and sub‑issues. Keep specs concise and avoid redundancy.

### Hard Rules

- Do not create or apply sprint labels. Do not apply pricing labels.
- Do not prefix titles with sprint codes (e.g., `[S1]`). Titles must be plain and descriptive.
- Do not add tasklists to parent issues; sub‑issues in the UI are the source of truth.
- Use real newlines in bodies (never literal `\n`).

### Minimal Spec Format (child issues)

- Title: descriptive (e.g., `Sorting: clickable headers with asc/desc`).
- Labels: apply exactly one time label (e.g., `Time: <2 Hours`) and one priority label (e.g., `Priority: 3 (High)`).
- Body:
  - First paragraph: one or two sentences describing the change.
  - `Acceptance:` section with short bullet criteria.
  - `Files:` section with bullet list of paths (optionally with starting line), e.g., `- src/web/app.ts:1`.

### Sprint Parent Issues

- Keep the body to the sprint spec only. No tasklists. No title prefixes.
- Link children using sub‑issues only (UI shows them automatically).

### Parent↔Child Linking (Sub‑issues)

- Use REST `sub_issues` endpoints (underscore). The child must be referenced by its REST numeric `id`.

List children:

```
gh api /repos/<REPO>/issues/<PARENT_NUMBER>/sub_issues -q .[].number
```

Add child:

```
child_num=16
rest_id=$(gh api /repos/<REPO>/issues/$child_num -q .id)
gh api -X POST -H "Accept: application/vnd.github+json" \
  /repos/<REPO>/issues/<PARENT_NUMBER>/sub_issues \
  -F sub_issue_id=$rest_id
```

Verify parent of a child:

```
gh api /repos/<REPO>/issues/<CHILD_NUMBER> -q .parent_issue_url
```

### Dependencies (optional)

- If needed, use REST `blocked_by` to express dependencies. Avoid tasklists for dependencies.

### Issue Dependencies (blocked_by / blocking)

Preferred: GraphQL API (works reliably on github.com). Use these standalone prompts (copy/paste) — no external files.

- Add “blocked by” using GraphQL `addBlockedBy`:
```
REPO=<OWNER/REPO>; TARGET=<issue number>; BLOCKER=<issue number>
issue_id=$(gh issue view -R "$REPO" $TARGET --json id -q .id)
blocker_id=$(gh issue view -R "$REPO" $BLOCKER --json id -q .id)
gh api graphql -f query="mutation { addBlockedBy(input: { issueId: \"$issue_id\", blockingIssueId: \"$blocker_id\" }) { issue { number title } blockingIssue { number title } } }"
```

- Remove “blocked by” using GraphQL `removeBlockedBy`:
```
REPO=<OWNER/REPO>; TARGET=<issue number>; BLOCKER=<issue number>
issue_id=$(gh issue view -R "$REPO" $TARGET --json id -q .id)
blocker_id=$(gh issue view -R "$REPO" $BLOCKER --json id -q .id)
gh api graphql -f query="mutation { removeBlockedBy(input: { issueId: \"$issue_id\", blockingIssueId: \"$blocker_id\" }) { issue { number title } } }"
```

- Read dependencies via GraphQL:
```
OWNER=<OWNER>; NAME=<REPO_NAME>; N=<issue number>
gh api graphql -f query="query { repository(owner: \"$OWNER\", name: \"$NAME\") { issue(number: $N) { blockedBy(first: 20) { nodes { number title } } blocking(first: 20) { nodes { number title } } } } }"
```

Notes
- REST endpoints for issue dependencies exist in docs, but may return 404 depending on token type/feature rollout. Prefer GraphQL for portability.

### Label Policy

- Do not create custom labels; read existing labels and choose from them.
- Allowed: exactly one time label (`Time: …`) and one priority label (`Priority: …`) per child issue.
- Disallowed: sprint labels, price labels, and ad‑hoc custom labels unless explicitly requested.
- Parents (sprint umbrella issues): do not set any time label to avoid double counting.

### Time Estimate Policy (Aggressive Defaults)

- Docs and small copy: `Time: <15 Minutes` (use LLM-assisted drafting and quick edits).
- Minor UI wiring (single header behavior, simple handler, or small filter): `Time: <1 Hour`.
- Moderate client work (URL state, drill-through, saved views, CSV export): `Time: <2 Hours`.
- Heavier but contained UI work (print stylesheet, lightweight charts, design tokens, a11y/keyboard, simple virtualization): `Time: <4 Hours`.
- Re-evaluate if scope expands; prefer aggressive estimates by default and adjust upward only with justification in the issue body.

title: Deadlines Incentive
body:
After a few calls with prospective pilot partners, it’s clear that teams care about **accurate time estimates** and **incentivizing deadlines**. This command should make deadlines more useful while rewarding contributors fairly.  

---

## **Objective**  
Build the **command-deadline plugin** to:  
1. **Encourage accurate time estimates** by tracking task durations.  
2. **Reward early completion** while ensuring deadlines matter.  

---

## **How It Works**  

### **Setting a Deadline**  
- Use `/deadline [date]` to set a deadline on a GitHub issue.  
- The deadline is tied to UTC by default but can be configured.  
- If a GitHub Project View is linked, the GitHub issue should sync there on the timeline view (if configured).  

### **Rewarding Early Completion**  
By default, finishing a task **on time** earns **100% of the task value**. If completed **faster**, the contributor gets a **speed bonus**. If **late**, they either receive **a reduced payout or are disqualified** (configurable).  

---

## **Deadline Reward Ratio Configuration**  

Instead of always giving **double the task value** for instant completion, we introduce a **configurable coefficient**:  

- **`deadlineRewardRatio`** → Controls how much of the task value is used for speed bonuses.  
- Default is `0.25`, meaning a max bonus of **25% extra** for instant completion.  
- If set to `1.0`, instant completion can **double** the reward.  

For example, on a **$1600** task with `deadlineRewardRatio = 0.25`:  
- **Instant completion** → `$1600 + $400 bonus = $2000`  
- **Halfway to deadline** → `$1600 + $200 bonus = $1800`  
- **On deadline** → `$1600` (no bonus, no penalty)  
- **Past deadline** → Payout gradually decreases unless disqualification is enabled.  

---

## **Final Reward Formula**  

```text
reward = baseTaskValue * max(0, 1 + (deadlineRewardRatio * (1 - (actualCompletionTime / assignedDeadline))) - ((1 - disqualificationEnabled) * (actualCompletionTime / assignedDeadline)))
```

### **How It Works**  
- **If completed early**, the reward increases up to `1 + deadlineRewardRatio` times the base task value.  
- **If completed exactly on time**, the reward is **1× task value**.  
- **If late**:
  - If **disqualification is enabled**, the reward drops to **0** at `assignedDeadline`.  
  - If **disqualification is disabled**, the reward **gradually decreases** until **0 at `2 * assignedDeadline`**.  

---

## **Disqualification (Optional)**  
If enabled, contributors **must** complete the task before the deadline or they receive **nothing**. This can be toggled per project.  

---

### **Mock YAML Configuration File**
Here’s a **sample `config.yml`** with all possible settings and their **default values**:

```yaml
commandDeadline:
  timezone: "UTC"  # Default timezone for deadlines (UTC, PST, etc.)
  deadlineRewardRatio: 0.25  # Max speed bonus (0.25 = 25% extra, 1.0 = 100% extra)
  disqualificationEnabled: true  # Whether missing the deadline results in a 0 reward
  projectView: null  # Link to GitHub Project View if deadlines should sync there
```

### **Configurable Behavior**
- If `deadlineRewardRatio = 0.5`, contributors **can earn up to 50% extra** for early completion.  
- If `disqualificationEnabled = false`, contributors **still get some payout even if late**, but it gradually declines.  
- If `projectView` is set, deadlines will be **synced to the linked GitHub Project View**.  

---

### **Final Summary**
- `/deadline [date]` sets a deadline.  
- **Early = Bonus** (configurable via `deadlineRewardRatio`).  
- **On time = Full payout**.  
- **Late = Configurable penalty (default: disqualification, or gradual payout reduction if disabled)**.  
- **Deadlines can sync to GitHub Project Views** if linked.  

This setup keeps the system **flexible, fair, and easy to configure**.

title: Pull/Task Matching

title: New Task Or Edit Pull Arbiter
body:
### Overview

- During pull requests, we need to have a bias of always moving forward. 
- We always need to make an active decision on whether to include requested changes in the current pull or if we should break them off into new tasks. 
- We should use an LLM to help us decide what to do. 

### Ideal Outcome

We seamlessly can review pulls and then the OS can intelligently create a new issue batching the requested changes and link back. Ideal if it can batch similar tasks aiming for between 1 hour and 1 day within the same GitHub issue (I think this is possible with my experience working with Claude 3.5 Sonnet.)

### Implementation

The way that this can work is if we leave the review state as "commented" and leave comments that seem like we want changes to be done. These will need to be understood by the OS. 

If we really think the changes are critical to be done in the current pull, then we must be sure to "request changes." 

### Remarks

I am concerned that it might be too quick to fire off new issues, so ideally we have it understand that there is a possibly already created "post pull request review" task, and to continue batching everything from the review in that task (we could standardize the naming scheme of the generated issue.) 

We may possibly need to check for pull request closed and merged to process the full conversation and fire off new tasks.  This will allow us room to determine the necessity of such suggestions.

`Fathom` Reports for "Communications Team" Management
Developer Referrals
body:
In order to increase the size of our developer community, we should pay who refer developers who contribute. Let's call them DevRels.

The vision is to generate a new permit for the DevRel upon task completion. 
- It is unclear to me exactly how to do default pricing (flat fee, percentage) 
- It can be easy to game and squeeze out extra rewards with a self referral unless the DevRel's cut is zero sum from the developer. If it is zero sum, then a percentage would be safest i.e. 5% or 10%. What is the highest percentage we can go before developers get annoyed? Perhaps we can also set a max cap, like 50 USD per reward in addition to the percentage. For example, if a developer receives a 1000 USD reward, perhaps the DevRel cap can be max 50 USD. 
- I fear the rewards may not be very competitive. We can consider high (non zero sum) rewards in the short term to kick things off, then switch it to zero sum mode later.
- We should also consider a reward for every developer referred (this may be implemented as a separate tool though, because it seems incompatible with the percentage or zero sum system)

### Configuration Requirements

- For version one, lets go only with percentages support. Make sure that the percentage is configurable. 
   - This will keep things simple in case the DevRel earns a tiny reward for leaving a small comment etc.
- Make sure that we can toggle zero sum mode (subtract from developer reward to pay the DevRel.) 

### Implementation Overview

We can do this in a couple of parts:
1. the new referral logs in with GitHub at `work.ubq.fi?ref=[github user id of DevRel]` 
2. we associate in a KV store the key being the DevRel GitHub ID and the value being an array of DevRel values. 
```typescript
type GitHubId = number;
type KV = { [key: GitHubId]: GitHubId[] };
```

This feels a little parasitic if a developer accidentally clicks a DevRel's link at some point in the future, especially if they start losing some of their rewards. I think we need some type of system to "undo" a referral. This doesn't feel like the right solution but I'm unsure what is. 

### Sybils
We can protect against sybils based on the age of a GitHub profile as well as a minimum XP requirement. For example, if the developer XP is low then the rewards are zero sum?
